digest: This case, initially flagged as a critical ransomware attack, has been identified as a scheduled and approved detection-validation exercise (CHG-4821) conducted in an isolated BUILD-LAB environment. All reported activities, including simulated malware execution, credential theft attempts, and C2 beaconing, were part of the test and confirmed to have no actual malicious impact or egress to production systems.

evidence_findings.title: Scheduled Detection Validation Exercise
evidence_findings.subject: Case Activity
evidence_findings.evidence: Case comments and artifact notes explicitly state this is a 'scheduled quarterly detection-validation exercise CHG-4821' approved by the SOC lead, scheduled from 13:00 through 14:00 UTC.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The reported activities are part of an approved and controlled simulation.

evidence_findings.title: Isolated Environment
evidence_findings.subject: Network and Hosts
evidence_findings.evidence: CMDB identifies both hosts as 'isolated cyber-range assets with no route to production.' Firewall confirms 'the isolated range blocked all external egress during the exercise.'
evidence_findings.conclusion: The simulated activities were contained within a non-production, isolated lab environment.

evidence_findings.title: No Actual Malicious Activity
evidence_findings.subject: Endpoint Activity
evidence_findings.evidence: EDR recorded 'simulation markers only: no file encryption, credential access, persistence, or payload download occurred.' The binary hash matches the 'internally signed validation tool inventory.'
evidence_findings.conclusion: Despite the alerts, no actual malicious actions (encryption, credential theft, persistence) took place on the endpoint.

evidence_findings.title: Approved Execution
evidence_findings.subject: User Activity
evidence_findings.evidence: Execution was initiated by service account 'svc_detection_test' under approved change 'CHG-4821'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The process execution was authorized and part of the approved exercise.

evidence_findings.title: Internal C2 Destination
evidence_findings.subject: Network Traffic
evidence_findings.evidence: The destination of the simulated C2 beacon traffic (10.250.0.10) is identified as 'the internal exercise controller'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: Simulated command and control traffic was directed to an internal, controlled asset, not an external malicious server.

attack_chain.description: Simulated execution of 'attack-simulator.exe' on BUILD-LAB-03 by the 'svc_detection_test' service account.
Simulated credential theft attempt as part of the ransomware scenario, but EDR confirmed no actual credential access occurred.
Simulated C2 beacon traffic from 10.250.0.23 to the internal exercise controller 10.250.0.10 on port 8443.
Simulated ransomware scenario, but EDR confirmed no file encryption or destructive actions took place.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Case created, marking the start of the simulated attack activities.
Analyst comment confirming the scheduled detection-validation exercise.

ioc_indicators.context: Internal exercise controller, destination of simulated C2.
Simulated source IP of C2 beacon traffic.
Approved service account used for initiating the simulation.
Approved change request for the detection validation exercise.

remediations.description: The reported activities were part of an approved and controlled detection-validation exercise in an isolated environment. No actual malicious activity or impact occurred.
